asDecan.p: Every sign gets split into three ten-degree slices, and each slice has its own planet and its own small card. Your Sun is in the last one of Pisces, from twenty to twenty-nine degrees, and the Golden Dawn hands that stretch to Mars. Pisces is mutable water, ruled by Jupiter in the old scheme and Neptune in the modern one, and it's the sign that soaks everything up. Mars has no special standing there. It's a visitor, not helped and not held back, and it takes on some of Jupiter's generosity while it stays. The first slice of Pisces belongs to Saturn and the Eight of Cups, the person walking away from something that isn't enough. The middle goes to Jupiter and the Nine, sitting back pleased with what's been gathered. Yours comes last, and it's already leaning toward Aries, which is where Mars feels at home. The Moon is your Sun card overall, and the Ten is the finer grain of it.

You're the one who actually does something about the feeling. A friend mentions over dinner that her rent's gone up again, and by the weekend you've sent her three listings and offered to drive her to the inspections. At a family Christmas where two of your siblings aren't talking, you're the one who seats them next to each other and then keeps the conversation going for two hours so it works. Someone at work gets left off the invite to the Friday drinks and you notice, and you quietly make sure they're on it next time. I see this a lot with late Pisces Suns. The softness everyone expects from the sign is there, you cry at adverts, but there's a bit of push under it that people don't see coming.

The lead already covers the warmth. What people take longer to see is that you can hold a group together through something rough without anyone quite noticing you're doing it. When a mate's father is in hospital for a month, you're the one who sets up the roster of who's bringing meals, and you do it in a group chat with a few jokes so it doesn't feel like an organisation. You also stand up for people, which surprises those who only know the gentle side. If someone talks down to the new girl at work, or to your kid's teacher at a school pickup, you'll say something, politely and without backing off. Mars gives Pisces a spine in this slice, and you tend to use it on someone else's behalf.

Past the obvious one, the moodiness, there's a harder shadow, and it's that you decide what everyone's happiness should look like and then work to make it happen. You book the family holiday, the cabin, the long lunch on the second day, and you're wounded when your teenager wants to stay in the room on their phone. You had a picture, and you pushed for it with real energy, and the picture didn't include anyone's actual mood. The other version is quieter. Your anger doesn't come out straight, because a lot of Pisces feels it shouldn't be angry at all, so it leaks. You go a bit cool with your partner after they forget to call, and when they ask, you say you're fine, and you keep saying it for about a week.

When something breaks, a relationship ending, a parent getting sick, being passed over for a role you'd earned, your first move is to look after everyone else. You're on the phone to your brother making sure he's all right before you've taken it in yourself. A week later the energy that was going outward has nowhere to go, and it tends to turn into either a lot of sleep or a sudden burst of doing, repainting the hallway, signing up for a course, picking a fight about the dishwasher that isn't about the dishwasher. The people close to you can find this confusing, because you seemed fine and then you weren't. What helps is getting the Mars side into your body. A hard swim, a long walk up a hill, and saying out loud to one person what you're actually angry about.

You love with a plan attached, which isn't what anyone expects from a Pisces. Within a few months you've started quietly building the life around the two of you, the friends they should meet, the Sunday routine, the idea of a dog. It's lovely to be on the receiving end of, mostly. The less obvious thing is that you find it hard to let a partner have a bad patch without trying to fix it. If they're flat and quiet after a rough month at work, you'll plan a weekend away, cook their favourite meal, suggest a counsellor, and then feel rejected when none of it lifts them. Sometimes they just want you to sit on the couch and not be doing anything about it. That takes practice for you.

You do your best work where there's a group of people to look after and a real aim to push toward. Nursing, teaching, running a café, social work, managing a small team that's had a bad run, even event work, anything where the mood of a place matters and someone has to hold it. You're good in a crisis at work because you stay kind while things are moving fast. Where it goes wrong is when you take the team's feelings as your job. You'll stay late smoothing over a row between two colleagues that the manager should have handled, and you'll do it for years without asking for the title or the money that goes with it. Asking for the pay rise is the Mars move you tend to skip.

At twenty this slice usually looks like a lot of feeling with the drive pointed at other people's lives. You're the friend who helps everyone move house and hasn't worked out what you want to study. The Mars side can be erratic, a burst of effort on a relationship or a cause and then a crash. By the mid-thirties most people with this placement have found something they're building, a family, a home, a practice, a circle of friends that's lasted, and the push steadies because it has somewhere to go. That's usually when the Ten of Cups feels most like you. The fifties tend to bring a loosening. The kids leave or the work settles, and I've seen a lot of late Pisces people start to spend that energy on themselves for the first time, and be quite surprised by what they want.

Once a week, before you do something for someone you love, check whether they've asked for it. If they haven't, ask them one question first, like whether they want help or just want to talk about it, and then do what they say, even if it's nothing. Keep a note on your phone of the times you held back. After a month, read it and see how many of those people were fine anyway.
